messages:
mike: Heads-up — need a new GPU node pool in us-west3 for low-latency multi-tenant inference. Quotas are tight, and we're seeing weird autoscaler behavior when spot nodes get preempted. Planning: mix of preemptible a10g for embeddings + a small h100 reserved pool for hot paths. Any sizing/CA flags recommendations? Also NAT egress limit per-subnet is 50, which could cause Pod setup failures under scale bursts.

sara: +1 on mixed pools. For us-west3 I’d target 4x h100 reserved (min 2, max 8) and a10g spot pool with max 40 but aggressive binpacking taints. Keep a small stable floor for the h100s.

jordan: Agree. Also watch kube-proxy conntrack and NAT ephemeral port exhaustion — if bursts create many short-lived pods you can hit egress limits. Might need a NAT gateway with higher port range or use multiple NAT IPs.

mike: Good call. Is there a recommended cluster-autoscaler config to avoid oscillation when spot evictions cause a ton of pending pods?

carla: We had success with these flags on CA:

```
--scale-down-unneeded-time=10m
--scale-down-utilization-threshold=0.45
--expander=least-waste
--max-empty-bulk-delete=2
--scale-down-delay-after-add=15m
```

That combination gives CA time to stabilize and prefers filling existing nodes.

jordan: Also consider pod disruption budgets (PDBs) and PriorityClasses so critical inference pods don't get immediately evicted when spot nodes disappear. For example, give hot-path pods priorityClass: high and set PDB minAvailable: 1.

mike: Nice. Any recommendations for nodepool sizing (cpu/ram per gpu) for a10g vs h100? Trying to minimize waste but avoid OOMs.

sara: For a10g (embedding workers) we use 8 vCPU / 64GB per GPU. Good balance for batch embeddings. For h100 (real-time) 16 vCPU / 192GB per GPU — keeps KV cache and concurrency healthy.

carla: Also tag nodepools with taints like `taint: inference=hot:NoSchedule` for h100 and `inference=warm:NoSchedule` for a10g. Use nodeSelector + tolerations on pod specs. Helps CA avoid shifting the wrong pods.

autoscaler-bot: Notice: cluster-autoscaler v1.23+ recommended. Metric: recent scale-up rate is 6 nodes / 5m, scale-down rate 1 node / 1m. High churn may be due to short spot lifetimes.

mike: On NAT: who owns the cloud infra change to add a second egress IP for the subnet? If we add one more NAT IP we should double the ephemeral port headroom. @carla can you run with cloud infra?

carla: I'll open a ticket to infra-provisioning. Quick workaround: use nodeLocalDNS + reduce ephemeral outbound calls during init (prewarm images). Also we can enable cluster egress policy to route heavy external calls through a different subnet with larger NAT.

jordan: One more ops trick: enable kubelet `--eviction-hard=memory.available<200Mi,nodefs.available<10%` and set `pod-termination-grace-period` higher for h100 pods so they get a chance to checkpoint KV cache.

mike: Thanks all. I'll draft a PR for the nodepool manifest and CA flags. Posting a draft snippet here for review: 

```
apiVersion: container.cnrm.cloud.google.com/v1beta1
kind: NodePool
metadata:
  name: infer-h100-reserved
spec:
  initialNodeCount: 2
  autoscaling:
    minNodeCount: 2
    maxNodeCount: 8
  config:
    machineType: n2-standard-16
    guestAccelerators:
    - acceleratorCount: 1
      acceleratorType: nvidia-h100
    taints:
    - key: inference
      value: hot
      effect: NO_SCHEDULE
```

Will put a matching a10g spot pool with `preemptible: true` and `maxNodeCount: 40`.

carla: Looks good. When you open the PR include tests for scale-up behavior in kuttl/job tests or a small e2e that simulates spot eviction. Also include notes about NAT limits in the PR description.

mike: Will do. Next step: PR by EOD, infra ticket for extra NAT IP, and we'll run a canary with 3 traffic lanes (low/medium/hot). :rocket: 

infra-bot: ticket #INFRA-4892 created for NAT egress IP increase in us-west3-subnet-a.
